title: Developer Construction — full rebuild specification
intro: A complete, precise description of every part of Excavatortron and exactly how it works, written so a developer with no prior context could rebuild the entire project from scratch. Read top to bottom. Each section is self-contained.

sections.title: 1. What Excavatortron is
sections.body:
Excavatortron is a self-running, self-improving dashboard that mines a YouTube playlist of AI videos and turns everything it finds — techniques (skills), products (tools), AI models, MCP connectors, slash commands, prompts, tips, and news — into a clean, searchable web dashboard.

It runs entirely in the cloud on free infrastructure and improves itself on a schedule, with no owner intervention and no paid cost beyond a Claude Pro subscription the owner already has.

The single source playlist: PLxtsVIUtYhNo6pY9FrVqVe2xh---Y8rxB (~1,100 videos).

Data flow in one line:  YouTube playlist -> fetch (metadata+transcript) -> analyze (extract structured data) -> dashboard (render data/*.json).  Around that core sit self-improvement, quality review, web discovery, and news stages.

sections.title: 2. Prime directive & hard constraints
sections.body:
PRIME DIRECTIVE: no owner intervention, and no new cost. 'Free' = public-repo GitHub Actions (unlimited free minutes) + the Claude Pro/Max SUBSCRIPTION token (not paid API billing) + free external API tiers that skip gracefully when absent.

HARD CONSTRAINTS (every change must honor):
- Never commit secrets. API keys live only in GitHub Actions secrets / local env vars; never printed, never committed.
- Never modify a FROZEN/starred record (slug in data/stars.json, or starred/locked:true). Max 10 stars; only the owner stars.
- Push automatically (the pipeline commits after every unit of work so a crash never loses progress).
- Output is English only; the SOURCE transcript is never edited (used verbatim).
- Never commit: make_icon.py, .claude/, OAuth client secrets (client_secret*.json), temp files. Stage explicit paths, never `git add -A`.
- The owner's Claude plan is Pro ($20) = a small weekly token bucket. Heavy work is night-gated (Israel time) and offloaded to FREE engines wherever possible.

sections.title: 3. Architecture (the cloud pipeline)
sections.body:
Everything is GitHub Actions workflows (.github/workflows/*.yml) on cron schedules, committing results back to the repo. The repo IS the database; the dashboard (GitHub Pages, served from repo root) reads ../data/*.json at runtime.

STAGES:
  fetch.yml       -> pull new playlist videos + metadata -> data/_pending/<id>.json
  transcribe.yml  -> caption backfill + Whisper ASR -> fills the transcript on pending records
  analyze.yml     -> Claude (CLAUDE.md) extracts -> skills/tools/models/connectors/commands/tips/prompts
  bulk_analyze.yml-> FREE multi-engine pool extracts the backlog (no Claude tokens)
  news.yml        -> 50 web RSS sources -> news feeds + digest
  improve.yml     -> weekly deep pass: dedup, calibrate, 50-question self-check, health
  review.yml      -> 3-agent quality gate (usability / cut-the-bullshit / deep-code-bugs)
  discover.yml    -> weekly web/GitHub/MCP tool discovery
  sources.yml     -> suggest new channels when the playlist stops growing
  codeql.yml      -> free static security scan
  claude.yml      -> lets the owner drive changes by commenting on GitHub

The ENGINES are Markdown specs (CLAUDE.md, IMPROVE.md, REVIEW.md, DISCOVER.md) that Claude follows in the cloud. They — not the Python — are the live extraction/curation logic.

sections.title: 4. The transcript pipeline (the #1 hard problem)
sections.body:
ROOT INSIGHT: you cannot extract a technique from a video's description — you need the spoken transcript. Early on, 99.7% of videos had NO transcript because YouTube BLOCKS the caption API (youtube-transcript-api) from datacenter IPs (GitHub Actions). So the cloud 'read' videos from their description only -> shallow, boilerplate output.

TWO-TIER TRANSCRIPT RECOVERY:
  Tier 1 (captions, fast, text-only, free): src/backfill_transcripts.py fetches the YouTube caption track. RULE: accept a caption ONLY if it is a COMPLETE full-video transcript — auto-generated captions span the whole video; a manual track is accepted only if it covers >=90% of the video duration. Otherwise the video is left for Whisper.
  Tier 2 (Whisper ASR, free, CPU): src/transcribe_local.py downloads the audio with yt-dlp and transcribes it with faster-whisper (tiny model, int8, no GPU). Runs in 'gaps' mode = only videos lacking an accepted complete caption.

WHERE THEY RUN: transcribe.yml runs both in the cloud (caption backfill works from cloud IPs for MOST videos via the transcript API's player-client path; Whisper runs on the runner's CPU/disk). The local residential runner (sync/fetch-runner.ps1) is a fallback that recovers captions YouTube blocks in the cloud. Whisper uses ZERO Claude tokens.

The transcript is stored verbatim on the pending record (transcript_source = 'transcript' | 'whisper' | 'description' | 'title').

sections.title: 5. The two analysis lanes (Pro-budget design)
sections.body:
Deep-reading ~1,100 transcripts with the Claude Pro token would blow the small weekly limit. So there are TWO lanes:

PREMIUM LANE (Claude, analyze.yml): follows CLAUDE.md exactly, highest quality, but NIGHT-GATED to the owner's Israel-time window (config.cadence.night_window 01:00-07:00) so it never drains his daytime quota. Reserved for incremental new videos + the improve/review curation.

FREE BULK LANE (bulk_analyze.yml + src/bulk_analyze.py): drains the backlog and any future burst using a POOL of FREE engines — zero Claude tokens. It round-robins across every engine whose key is set (their daily quotas ADD UP):
  - Claude Sonnet 4.6 via GitHub Models (= actual Claude quality, free, ~50/day)  [secret GH_MODELS_TOKEN]
  - GPT-OSS 120B via Cerebras (near-frontier, free, ~1M tokens/day)               [secret CEREBRAS_API_KEY]
  - Gemini 2.5 Flash (good, free, ~1,500/day)                                      [secret EXTERNAL_REVIEW_API_KEY]
Each engine call sends the transcript + the CLAUDE.md extraction rules (anti-boilerplate, skills-vs-tools) and gets back strict JSON; deterministic Python then MERGES it into the data files (dedup by slug/name, union endorsement_video_ids).

ANTI-BOILERPLATE GATE (the #1 quality rule): never emit a skill that is a bare vendor name ('Claude', 'ChatGPT') or a template like 'Using X for productivity'. A skill must be a SPECIFIC method shown in the video. If a video only mentions a product, it becomes a TOOL, not a skill.

sections.title: 6. Skills vs Tools (the #1 content rule)
sections.body:
SKILL = a technique / workflow — something you DO (e.g. 'Claude Agent Loop', 'Nano-Banana image pipeline'). Lives in data/skills.json and a SKILL.md package folder.
TOOL = a product / model / app / service — something that EXISTS (e.g. 'Cursor', 'Gemini 2.5 Pro', 'n8n'). Lives in data/tools.json.
MODEL = a subset of tools (an AI model with a version) mirrored into data/models.json with a per-category podium.
CONNECTOR = an MCP server / integration -> data/connectors.json.

SKILL.md FOLDER ROUTING (one folder PER tool):
  target_tool == 'claude'  -> skills/<slug>/SKILL.md      (syncs to Desktop 'claude skills of eitan')
  any other tool           -> other-skills/<tool>/<slug>/SKILL.md  (syncs to '<tool> skills of eitan')
The sync (sync/sync-skills.ps1) also copies skills/ into ~/.claude/skills/ so every new Claude Code chat can load them.

sections.title: 7. The engine specs (the Markdown brains)
sections.body:
These Markdown files ARE the live logic; Claude reads and obeys them in the cloud.

CLAUDE.md (analyze engine): Step 1 pick up data/_pending batch; Step 2 relevance gate; Step 2b video-quality score (1-10, recency penalty); Step 2c follow AI-relevant description links with WebFetch and mine them; Step 2d use the 'surroundings' (top comments, stats, tags); Step 2e comment-gated resources; Step 3 extract SKILLS; Step 3b extract TOOLS (extract EVERY named tool); Step 3c extract PROMPTS; Step 4 models ranking; Steps 5-8 improvement/tips/commands/news/connectors; commit + push after EACH video.

IMPROVE.md (weekly deep pass): Step 0 load state + decide run mode (catch-up light / idle / full); Step 0c extraction-completeness (top priority — re-queue thin videos); Step 1/1b apply approved suggestions + self-check fix tasks; Step 2 data hygiene/dedup/index; Steps 3-7b near-dup, ratings, stars, UX self-review, skills-folder learning, dynamic tabs, feed health; Step 7c the 50-question reference self-check (ALWAYS runs); Step 8 health report; Step 9 audit.

REVIEW.md (3-agent quality gate): Claude reviews first across usability (benchmarked vs competitors) + 'cut the bullshit' + deep code bugs; then src/external_review.py asks a DIFFERENT engine (Gemini) for a second opinion (graceful-skip); CodeQL is the automated deep-code arm.

DISCOVER.md (web tool discovery): weekly, finds AI tools NOT already in tools.json from GitHub Trending + awesome-lists (incl. awesome-mcp-servers) + Product Hunt + web search; strong MCP/open-source emphasis; flags upcoming (unreleased) tools.

sections.title: 8. The cloud workflows (.github/workflows)
sections.body:
Each is a cron + a job that commits results. Key wiring:
- All use a concurrency group so two of the same never overlap.
- Claude steps use anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 with claude_code_oauth_token = secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_REAL (the Pro subscription token).
- The safety-net commit step runs `if: always()` and (critical fix) sets the git remote URL with secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN before pushing — otherwise the push fails with 'Invalid username or token'.
- analyze.yml has a Plan step that night-gates heavy runs (zoneinfo Asia/Jerusalem) and respects catch-up mode.
- transcribe.yml: Step 1 caption backfill (youtube-transcript-api) then Step 2 Whisper (faster-whisper). Stdlib + pip installs on the runner.
- bulk_analyze.yml: stdlib only, passes the 3 engine secrets as env, round-robins the pool.
Schedules (UTC): fetch frequent; transcribe every 4h; analyze every 3h (night-gated); bulk every 3h; news every 6h; improve Sat 20:00 + first-week nightly; review Sat 23:00 + first-week nightly; discover Sun 01:00; sources daily.

sections.title: 9. The Python scripts (src/)
sections.body:
fetch.py — pulls playlist items via the YouTube Data API (YOUTUBE_API_KEY), the transcript (youtube-transcript-api), full description, resolved links, view/like/comment stats, tags, duration, and top comments; writes data/_pending/<id>.json.
backfill_transcripts.py — caption recovery with the COMPLETE-caption rule (auto-gen, or manual >=90% coverage); leaves the rest for Whisper. No API key needed.
transcribe_local.py — Whisper ASR (faster-whisper, tiny, int8) on yt-dlp audio; 'gaps' mode.
bulk_analyze.py — the free multi-engine extraction pool (Gemini + OpenAI-compatible: GitHub Models / Cerebras); deterministic merge.
news.py — 50 RSS/Atom sources -> windowed feeds + a heuristic 'most important' digest.
external_review.py — Gemini second-opinion for REVIEW.md (graceful-skip).
requeue.py — re-queue shallow/boilerplate videos for deep re-analysis.
suggest_channels.py — detect playlist-growth stall (<25/week) -> propose a high-value channel + 20 of its videos.
add_to_playlist.py + oauth_setup.py — one-time Google OAuth so approved channel videos are added to the playlist.
merge_dupes.py — dedup helper. (Dead/legacy: process_video.py, analyze_batch.py.)

sections.title: 10. The data files (data/)
sections.body:
CONTENT: skills.json {videos_seen[], skills[]}; tools.json {tools[]}; models.json {category: {podium,full_ranking}}; connectors.json; commands.json; tips.json {by_tool, general}; prompts.json {prompts[]}; dev_construction.json (this doc).
NEWS: daily/weekly/monthly_news.json + _web variants; web_news_store.json; feeds_health.json. Each window file has header {window, covered_from/to, digest[]} + entries[].
STATE: status.json (run report, counters, analyze_ok, last_analyze); index.json (compact slug->score map); catch_up.json; _pending/ + processed/ (per-video work files); review_state.json (first-week anchor).
SELF-IMPROVE/REVIEW: self_check.json (50 Q results + score); improvement_tasks.json; improvement_suggestions.json; approvals.json; improvement_audit.json; health.json; review_findings.json; tab_candidates.json + extra_tabs.json (dynamic tabs).
DISCOVERY/SOURCES: discovery_log.json; channel_suggestions.json; source_growth.json; comment_gated.json.
HOUSEKEEPING: deleted_skills.json (pre-delete snapshots); merge_log.json; stars.json (frozen records).

sections.title: 11. The dashboard (docs/)
sections.body:
Vanilla JS, no build step. index.html (UI shell + CSS) + dashboard.js (renders every tab) + sw.js (service worker shell cache; bump SHELL_CACHE to force refresh) + manifest.webmanifest (PWA) + icon.png.

CRITICAL: dashboard.js fetches ../data/*.json, so GitHub Pages MUST serve the WHOLE REPO from root (Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> main -> / root). A root index.html redirects the bare URL to docs/.

TABS: Skills Library, Tool Rating (merged tools+models, podium per category + 'what it does' + model filter), Coming Soon (release_status='upcoming'), Prompts (master/guardrail/creation, one-click copy), Improvement Log, Tips & Commands, News Feed (digest pinned on top), Connectors, Grow Sources (channel suggestions + comment-walled list), Self-Improvement (50-Q self-check + 3-agent review), Developer Construction (this). Plus a Quick-read toggle that condenses every tab, and auto-created Dynamic Tabs (NEW badge auto-expires).

sections.title: 12. The self-improvement loop
sections.body:
Each weekly deep pass (improve.yml) RETURNS TO THE OWNER'S REFERENCE SPEC (docs/REFERENCE_SPEC.md Part C = 50 yes/no questions) and answers all 50 against live data -> data/self_check.json {score, results[{n,question,answer,evidence}]}. Every 'no' opens a task in improvement_tasks.json {n,fix,kind: safe_auto|needs_approval|engine_followup}. Next run, Step 1b auto-applies the safe ones. The dashboard shows 'Self-check score X/50'.

Autonomy is split (config.self_improvement.autonomy = safe_auto_suggest_risky): safe ops apply automatically; risky ops become suggestions in improvement_suggestions.json that the owner approves via the offline MCP server (mcp_server/server.py: approve_suggestion, approve_channel, star_skill, run_improve, ...) or by commenting on GitHub. Caps bound changes/run; a token budget keeps cost down; frozen records are never touched.

HIGHER FIRST-WEEK ITERATION: improve + review run nightly for the first 7 days (anchored in review_state.json.first_run_at), then fall back to weekly.

sections.title: 13. Rebuild from scratch (step by step)
sections.body:
1. Create a PUBLIC GitHub repo (public = free unlimited Actions).
2. Add the files: config.json, the 4 engine .md specs, src/*.py, .github/workflows/*.yml, docs/* (dashboard), data/ (seed empty/curated), brain/ (Obsidian vault).
3. Add GitHub Actions SECRETS: YOUTUBE_API_KEY (fetch); CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_REAL (Pro token via `claude setup-token`, renew ~yearly); EXTERNAL_REVIEW_API_KEY (Gemini free); GH_MODELS_TOKEN (a GitHub PAT, free Claude Sonnet via GitHub Models); CEREBRAS_API_KEY (free); optional YOUTUBE_OAUTH_* (playlist auto-add).
4. Enable GitHub Pages: Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> main -> / (root). The dashboard serves at <user>.github.io/<repo>/docs (the root index.html redirects there).
5. Set config.playlist_id to your playlist. The crons start on schedule; trigger any stage now with `gh workflow run <name>.yml` or the Actions 'Run workflow' button.
6. (Optional, residential IP) Run sync/setup-sync.ps1 once to register the local fetch/transcribe runner + Desktop mirror.
That's the whole system: free, self-running, self-improving.

sections.title: 14. Gotchas & hard-won lessons
sections.body:
- YouTube blocks the caption API AND throttles audio from datacenter IPs -> use the complete-caption rule + Whisper + a residential fallback.
- The safety-net `git push` in a workflow fails ('Invalid username or token') unless you reset the remote URL with secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN first.
- GitHub reserves the GITHUB_ secret-name prefix -> use GH_MODELS_TOKEN.
- GitHub Pages must serve the REPO ROOT (dashboard reads ../data), not /docs.
- Google AI Studio (Gemini) requires the account to be 18+/verified; GitHub Models + Cerebras do not.
- On a Pro plan the 5 Claude workflows fight one small weekly bucket -> night-gate analyze, offload bulk to free engines, keep improve/review weekly.
- Anti-boilerplate gate is essential: without it, dedup collapses ~950 'Claude/ChatGPT' vendor stubs and the library looks empty.
- Never auto-comment on YouTube to harvest gated files (ToS violation -> account ban, and the files usually arrive by DM anyway). Resolve gated resources by searching the creator's PUBLIC footprint + web instead.
